name: TypeScript full-stack web application on Node
use_cases: Browser applications with owned APIs and relational data
choose_when: Shared TypeScript contracts and React UI are useful
Server rendering or a web-facing backend is required
Team accepts explicit server/client and cache boundaries
avoid_when: Only static editorial content is required
Existing API already owns all backend responsibilities and SSR is unnecessary
Native mobile or desktop UI is the deliverable

alternatives: Preserve existing pnpm
Bun after compatibility validation
tools.reason: LTS production policy and reproducible dependency install
tools.limits: Pin resolved runtime/dependencies; latest is a scaffold-time lookup, not a CI dependency strategy

tools.default: Next.js App Router + React + strict TypeScript
alternatives: React/Vite for API-backed SPA
TanStack Start for typed route loaders/server functions
Astro for editorial sites
tools.reason: Full-stack React with version-matched agent documentation
tools.limits: TanStack Start official homepage labelled RC at review; web UI is not native UI; framework does not supply business correctness

tools.default: README navigation + generated version-matched agent guidance
alternatives: README-only workflow when the repository explicitly chooses it
tools.reason: Keep repository instructions and installed framework documentation discoverable
tools.limits: Honor existing instruction ownership. Optional README-only policy: scaffold with --no-agents-md and set agentRules:false before next dev; neither is required by this stack.

tools.default: Next.js development MCP endpoint with real browser inspection
alternatives: Existing development logs and browser tooling when MCP is unavailable
tools.reason: Combine version-matched framework context, compilation errors, routes and runtime logs with the actual rendered application.
tools.limits: Development only. Inspect the installed Next.js and next-devtools-mcp versions before configuring tools. Some runtime inspection requires an open browser session; Turbopack compilation tools have their own constraints. Framework tools do not replace authorization tests or real browser verification. Do not install optional skills or enable automatic upgrades merely to read this reference.
tools.setup: Follow the installed-version MCP guide to connect a selected agent client to the existing dev server; keep the endpoint and development credentials private. Use the project-selected browser verification route.

alternatives: Existing compatible runtime schema library
tools.reason: Runtime schemas with inferred TypeScript types
tools.limits: Validate requests/environment/external results; shape checks do not establish permission or truth

alternatives: Existing database/ORM conventions
tools.reason: Typed schema with inspectable SQL history
tools.limits: Configure schema paths and target environment; apply migration once; rehearse fresh DB and forward compatibility

alternatives: Existing identity provider or auth library matching requirements
tools.reason: Integrated session/provider support without designing password/session primitives
tools.limits: Auth schema generate then Drizzle migrations; direct Better Auth migrate is Kysely-only; configure origin/secrets/recovery; authorize near data

alternatives: Omit for request-local work
Existing durable queue/workflow service
tools.reason: Checkpointed steps, retries and waits
tools.limits: Idempotent effects and authorized approvals required; use outbox for DB/event consistency; avoid beta durable endpoints as default

alternatives: Preserve an existing TypeScript configuration after checking its guarantees
tools.reason: Independent deterministic checks for generated edits
tools.limits: Next build does not run lint; never ignore build/type errors to satisfy a check

alternatives: Biome when project has selected it
tools.reason: Independent deterministic checks for generated edits
tools.limits: Next build does not run lint; never ignore build/type errors to satisfy a check

alternatives: Existing suitable test suite
tools.reason: Run isolated domain behavior checks with a configured test environment
tools.limits: Install/configure Vitest and DOM environment for UI tests. Next async Server Components require browser/integration coverage instead.

alternatives: Existing suitable test suite
tools.reason: Test rendered components through user-visible DOM behavior
tools.limits: Install @testing-library/react and its @testing-library/dom peer; configure the test runner/DOM environment. This is a component utility library, not a test runner.

alternatives: Existing suitable test suite
tools.reason: Exercise critical journeys in actual browser engines
tools.limits: Install @playwright/test and matching browsers; configure an isolated test server/data and test session expiry, routing and authorization failures.

alternatives: Verified adapter
Static export for compatible static subset
tools.reason: Documented full Next feature support with Node/Docker
tools.limits: Adapters vary; verify chosen host, secrets, DB connections, sessions, migrations and restore; Cloudflare needs separate compatibility review

tools.default: TanStack Query for client-owned remote state
alternatives: Next server loading for server-owned data
Router loaders for simple route data
tools.reason: Queries, mutations and invalidation support interactive API screens
tools.limits: Install @tanstack/react-query and provide QueryClient. Define tenant-aware keys, staleTime/retry policy and clear session data on sign-out; in Next prefer server loading until a client cache has a job.

tools.default: React Hook Form for complex client forms
alternatives: Native HTML forms for simple submissions
tools.reason: Separates client form state and validation from page components
tools.limits: Install react-hook-form only where needed; wire existing runtime schemas deliberately. Render accessible labels/errors; validate and authorize submissions on the server.

tools.default: Tailwind CSS when utility styling fits the project
alternatives: CSS Modules or existing CSS design system
tools.reason: Reusable styling without a runtime component dependency
tools.limits: For Vite install tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite, add the plugin and CSS import. Use the framework-specific installation path for Next; retain established styles when present.

alternatives: Semantic native HTML controls
tools.reason: Provides focus and keyboard behavior for common interaction patterns
tools.limits: Install only used components. Authors still supply names, contrast and meaningful composition; verify keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.

tools.default: axe-core through Playwright + manual keyboard review
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Automated audits identify common accessibility defects in real pages
tools.limits: Install @axe-core/playwright; scan representative states and use a screen reader/keyboard. Passing automated rules is not complete accessibility evidence.

alternatives: Provider-supported SDK when API-specific features are required
tools.reason: SMTP transport avoids coupling email templates to a hosting vendor
tools.limits: Install nodemailer; configure server-only transport, verified sender and TLS. Test locally, queue required delivery, handle ambiguous results and bounces; SMTP acceptance is not inbox delivery. Verify the resolved Nodemailer release supports the pinned Node runtime and preserves TLS certificate validation.

tools.default: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 S3 client
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Object storage separates durable files from ephemeral application disks
tools.limits: Install @aws-sdk/client-s3; authorize object keys, restrict size/type and configure lifecycle. Keep credentials server-side; add presigner only for direct uploads and validate provider compatibility.

alternatives: WebSocket service for bidirectional collaboration
Polling for infrequent updates
tools.reason: Browser-standard streaming suits status/progress feeds
tools.limits: Backend owns authenticated stream and event IDs. Test reconnect, replay and proxy buffering; EventSource is one-way and its constructor offers no arbitrary authorization-header option. Confirm long-lived connection support on host.

setup_steps: Start in an external source repository parent in a local development workspace with runtime, identity, database and host requirements documented.

Run npx create-next-app@latest my-app --ts --eslint --app --src-dir --use-npm; review prompts; enter my-app; record resolved versions. Add --no-agents-md only for a repository that explicitly opts out of generated agent files.

Preserve generated agent guidance and put purpose, commands, environment names and installed-documentation navigation in README. For an explicit README-only repository policy, set agentRules:false before next dev.
Confirm strict TypeScript. Install npm install zod drizzle-orm pg better-auth server-only and npm install -D drizzle-kit @types/pg dotenv; add inngest only for required durable work.
Configure server-only database/auth modules and Drizzle PostgreSQL schema/config, development DATABASE_URL, auth secret/base URL and Next route/client integration.
Run npx auth@latest generate; include generated schema in Drizzle paths; run npx drizzle-kit generate; review SQL; apply npx drizzle-kit migrate only to verified development DB.

Install npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths @playwright/test; configure unit/UI environments and production Playwright webServer; run npx playwright install.
Implement invalid-input, tenant ownership, session and critical browser tests. Register durable workflow endpoint/worker only if used; exercise retries and duplicate events.
Rehearse migrations on fresh test DB, run checks, configure chosen host and single migration job; inspect production session/browser behavior and rollback compatibility.

open_questions: Does the product require server-rendered routes, client-owned state, or both?
Which identity providers, account recovery and SSO requirements must be supported?
Which host, database connection budget and migration/restore process will own production?
Which workflows need retries, email, object storage or persistent realtime connections?

Run npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts; enter my-app; npm install; record resolved versions and commit lockfile.
